chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
“You shouldn't sell in winter.” Really? In Quebec, winter has its particularities, but it also offers real opportunities, whether you're buying or selling. This guide separates the myths from reality.

You'll see the pros and cons of each season, and how to take advantage of winter rather than fear it.

Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

chapters.title: The Myth of the “Wrong Season”
chapters.objective: Adding nuance to the received wisdom.
chapters.html:
Adding nuance to the received wisdom.

There are generally fewer properties for sale and fewer buyers in winter. But “fewer” doesn't mean “worse”: winter buyers are often more serious and motivated, and competition among sellers is lower.

The result: a good property that's well prepared and well priced can sell very well in winter, sometimes with less competition.

Émilie's tip

Don't delay a sale just “because it's winter.” A buyer who visits in January at -15°C is rarely a tourist: they're motivated. Fewer buyers, but often more serious ones.

chapters.title: Selling in Winter: Presenting Well
chapters.html:
Offsetting the season's challenges.

  • Clear snow and ice: safe, welcoming access.
  • Maximize the light (short days): open the curtains, turn on the lights, use warm bulbs.
  • Warmth and atmosphere: a well-heated, cozy home is reassuring.
  • Photos: also use summer images of the grounds, if available.

Winter highlights comfort and energy efficiency: put them front and centre.

Émilie's tip

In winter, sell comfort: a warm, well-lit home that's easy to access despite the snow. Also show what the grounds look like in summer with a few photos.

chapters.title: Buying in Winter: Opportunities
chapters.objective: Taking advantage of the buyer-side benefits.
chapters.html:
Taking advantage of the buyer-side benefits.

Buying in winter often means less competition among buyers and motivated sellers (sometimes in a hurry). It's also a chance to see how the property performs in deep cold: insulation, heating, leaks, snow removal, ice.

You're testing the home in its most demanding conditions — a not-insignificant inspection advantage.

Émilie's tip

Buying in winter lets you see the home at its worst: drafts, ice, real heating costs. What you notice in January won't catch you by surprise the following winter.

chapters.title: Action Plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, in concrete terms.

This week

  1. Decide on my strategy without seasonal bias.
  2. List the winter adjustments (snow removal, lighting).

Within 30 days

  1. Prepare a warm, accessible presentation.
  2. Take advantage of a less crowded market.

After that

  1. Act based on my needs, not the calendar.

chapters.title: Resources & Glossary
chapters.html:
• Seasonality: variation in market activity depending on the season.
  • Motivated buyers: those who visit in winter, often more serious.
  • Winter curb appeal: cleared access and a warm presentation.
  • Winter test: observing insulation, heating, and leaks in deep cold.
  • Seller competition: lower in winter.
